pages.text: "Beans, go away!" Lulu pushed beans and spinach to the plate's edge. The cousins ate side by side at the big table. Only cheese remained in Lulu's plate center.
"Cheese alone fills me up!" Lulu ate only cheese. Mom watched quietly from the kitchen. The beans and spinach stayed at the edge.
Next morning, Lulu kept falling behind on the hill path. Three cousins ran ahead. Lulu walked as if dragging the hind legs. "Why have I no energy?"
Mom brought Lulu to the kitchen table. She arranged foods in a ring on a big plate. "Look, Lulu. A ring on your plate!"
Round tomatoes, long carrots, square cheese—all in a circle. But one bean place was empty. The ring broke there.
Mom whispered, "Fill the gap to finish the ring." Lulu set one bean in the empty place. The circle was complete.
A tomato bite, a carrot bite, a cheese bite, then crunch—the last bean! "Oh! Tasty! Round the plate—eat it all!"
The dragging hind legs bounced. Lulu stretched both forepaws high and hopped. The blue bell jingled. "My energy is back!"
At dinner, Lulu brought a plate first. "One, arrange a ring of different foods! Two, fill the gaps! Three, a bite from each, round the plate!" The cousins made rings too.
Mom kissed Lulu's cheek and patted the back. Eating all round the plate gives you energy. "Make a ring tomorrow too, Mom! Round the plate—eat it all!"
